articles.title: Uk Work Placements: UK govt pledges 300,000 new work placements as NEET numbers top one million | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government announced plans to provide 300,000 new work experience and training opportunities over the next three years. The initiative, backed by major employers including Manchester Airport and Gatwick Airport, will offer placements in sectors like construction, hospitality, health and social care.  Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden stated that practical workplace experience is crucial for young people's long-term career prospects. A review led by Alan Milburn found limited access to work experience as a major barrier for young jobseekers.

articles.title: How the end of the nuclear file could reshape Iran, and the region | Nuclear Weapons | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A debate is underway in Tehran over whether control of the Strait of Hormuz can replace uranium enrichment as Iran's deterrent.  Iran’s decision to close the strait has led to US countermeasures, including a naval blockade. The immediate global impact, surging oil prices, and market shocks have surprised even Iran, prompting internal debate about its domestic political consequences. Since 2005, Iran's nuclear program has been a source of political repression and division, but recent events suggest a shift away from nuclear latency towards maritime control.  The new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, has not mentioned the nuclear program in public statements, instead emphasizing Iran’s right to govern the Strait of Hormuz. Some conservative factions are now advocating for a suspension of enrichment and a pivot toward maritime control, arguing that it offers more leverage than nuclear latency. This shift could weaken hardliners' justification for purging reformers and open space for elected offices and civil society.

articles.title: Vladimir Putin: Gene therapy, mini-pigs, organ printing: Inside Putin's $26 billion quest to beat aging - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin and his inner circle are investing heavily in antiaging science through a $26 billion state initiative called “New Health Preservation Technologies.” The program includes gene therapy, organ printing, and cryotherapy, all aimed at extending human lifespan.  This initiative is driven by Putin, who has expressed fascination with immortality and the potential for humans to continuously repair and replace body parts. While Russia's efforts have produced ambitious claims, some experts question their scientific validity due to limited peer-reviewed research and sanctions hindering collaboration with Western institutions. The Kremlin's interest in antiaging science extends beyond laboratories, reflecting anxieties about aging and a desire to maintain power in the face of mortality.

articles.title: Kenyan court suspends US Ebola quarantine facility plan | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Kenyan court has suspended a plan to establish an Ebola quarantine facility for US nationals exposed to the virus, following a legal challenge by rights activists. The proposed arrangement, intended to isolate and monitor potentially exposed individuals in Kenya rather than transport them home, was met with backlash from health workers and concerns about public health risks.  The Kenyan government has acknowledged discussions with US officials over Ebola preparedness efforts but has not directly addressed the reports of a quarantine facility. The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that the outbreak in eastern DRC is heavily concentrated, hampered by conflict and displacement, and could spread undetected for longer periods before being identified.

articles.title: IHC to hear Imaan, Hadi's sentence suspension pleas in social media posts case on June 1 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has set June 1st for hearing the sentence suspension applications filed by human rights lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha in a social media posts case. The court received a certified copy of the Supreme Court’s May 12th order, which directed the IHC to decide on their pleas within two weeks.  The couple has been in jail since January after being arrested for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. Their sentences were handed down by a sessions court just a day after the development, prompting criticism from rights bodies, politicians, and journalists.

articles.title: US Treasury secretary confirms plans for $250 bill featuring Trump’s face | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent confirmed plans for a new $250 bill featuring President Donald Trump's face, pending legislation that would allow current and former presidents to appear on US currency.  The proposed design, which is in anticipation of a change in law, was created by Treasurer Brandon Beach, a Trump appointee, with the intention of marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. The Treasury Department has not yet responded to requests for comment.

articles.title: Italy Heatwave: Italy on red alert as France, Portugal beat hottest May day record - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Italy, Portugal, and France issued warnings as a heatwave brought record-breaking temperatures to Europe.  The mercury peaked at 40.3C in Portugal, surpassing the previous record of 40C from May 2001, while Britain and France reported their hottest-ever May days. The heatwave has caused hospitalisations in Portugal and deaths attributed to drowning accidents in both Britain and France.  The European meteorological agency warned that the heatwave is likely to last into early June.

articles.title: A 2,000-year-old stone found in Karnak temple reveals a Roman emperor hidden in the form of an Egyptian pharaoh | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Egypt’s Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, in collaboration with an Egyptian-French archaeological team, has uncovered hidden layers beneath the northern wall gate associated with Ramses III at the Karnak temples. The project revealed reused stones from earlier dynasties, suggesting that the gate was built using material from older monuments, creating a kind of architectural archive.  The excavations also unearthed construction phases spanning multiple periods, including Roman and Byzantine eras, indicating a dynamic religious landscape that evolved over time. A sandstone stela depicting Emperor Tiberius in traditional pharaonic style, found near the gate, suggests how Roman authority was integrated into existing religious systems.

articles.title: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket explodes on launchpad in Florida | Science and Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket exploded on a test launchpad in Florida, the latest setback for the company's space venture. The incident occurred during a hot-fire test and caused a massive fireball that sent smoke billowing into the air. Jeff Bezos, founder of Blue Origin, stated that the cause is still unknown but personnel are safe.  Mike Haridopolos, US House Representative from Florida, expressed gratitude for no injuries and commended first responders.

articles.title: Israel, Russia added to UN blacklist on sexual violence in conflicts - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations has added Israel and Russia to its annual list of groups suspected of systematic sexual violence in conflict. The report, published annually by the UN, documented incidents in Ukraine and the occupied Palestinian territories, including rape, genital mutilation, and torture against Palestinians detained by Israeli authorities.  Israel responded with a freeze on relations with the UN secretary-general's office until the end of his term, while Russia was also accused of sexual violence against prisoners of war in occupied Ukrainian territories and within Russia itself.

articles.title: Netanyahu says he has directed IDF to increase control of Gaza to 70%
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, announced a directive to increase Israel's control of Gaza to 70%, contradicting the ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025.  This expansion comes as Israel continues strikes on Gaza despite the truce and stalled negotiations for the implementation of the Trump-led peace plan. Israel Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel pledged to eliminate Hamas leaders, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich have defended what they call a "voluntary migration" of Palestinians from Gaza, which could be considered forced displacement. At least 738 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.

articles.title: Meet Antoine Moses: Canadian ‘tree lover’ sets a second Guinness World Record by planting 47,460 trees in just 24 hours on the Kenyan coast | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Antoine Moses, a Canadian tree planter, set a new record by planting 47,460 mangrove saplings in a single day on the Kenyan coast.  This follows his previous record of 23,000 trees planted in northern Alberta in 2021. Moses's work focuses on endurance planting and pushing the limits of speed within tightly measured time windows. He has previously planted over a million trees across various projects, demonstrating a dedication to large-scale reforestation efforts.  The Kenyan planting effort was part of a larger project aimed at restoring mangroves in Mombasa, which are crucial for coastal stability and fishing communities.

articles.title: Mexico backs amendment to annul election results over foreign interference | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Mexican lower house approved a constitutional amendment that would allow for the nullification of elections in cases of foreign interference. The proposal, which defines foreign interference as various actions like financing, propaganda, and digital manipulation, passed with 307 votes in favor, 128 against, and one abstention.  However, the amendment still requires Senate approval to take effect and faces criticism from opposition lawmakers who argue it undermines confidence in the electoral process and could be used to contest legitimate results. The ruling Morena party defended the measure as a necessary safeguard of Mexico's democracy.

articles.title: Dar arrives in Washington to meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio: FO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, arrived in Washington to meet with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.  The meeting will focus on bilateral relations, regional and global developments, and cooperation in key sectors. The visit comes amid reports that US and Iranian negotiators are close to a deal extending their fragile ceasefire for 60 days.  Dar is expected to leave Washington later in the day after wrapping up his engagements.

articles.title: Ukraine war: Russian drone crashes into Romanian apartment block
articles.rephrased_article: A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in Galati, Romania, causing a fire and injuring two people. The incident occurred as Russia continues attacks near the Ukrainian border. Russia has not commented on the incident, but Romania's foreign ministry condemned it as an "escalation" and requested increased anti-drone capabilities from NATO.  The incident comes amid ongoing drone attacks in Ukraine, including one that targeted the port of Izmail.

articles.title: Friday briefing: ​What do the cuts in aid mean for the fight against Ebola in the DRC? | Ebola | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ebola is spreading rapidly in eastern DRC and Uganda, claiming at least 240 lives since the outbreak began. The virus, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids, has been difficult to contain due to a lack of testing facilities and a fragile relationship between healthcare workers and the local community.  The outbreak is being exacerbated by ongoing conflict and limited resources. Medical staff are struggling to save lives as they face attacks from angry families and a shortage of protective equipment. The US, which has significantly reduced its humanitarian aid to the region since 2017, is facing criticism for its inadequate response.  Experts warn that without increased funding and support, containing the outbreak will be challenging.

articles.title: Federal jury finds army veteran and two other ICE protesters guilty of conspiracy | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A federal jury in Spokane, Washington found three protesters guilty of felony conspiracy charges for their role in a June 2025 protest against ICE. The defendants, including a US military veteran, face potential sentences of up to six years in prison and a $250,000 fine.  They are expected to appeal the verdict, which has drawn national attention and criticism from legal experts who argue it sets a dangerous precedent for limiting free speech. Richard Barker, former acting US attorney for Eastern Washington state, resigned rather than sign the indictment, expressing concerns about the case's impact on First Amendment rights.

articles.title: 'Act of terror': Man stabs 3 at Swiss train station, arrested - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of journalists, provides global news and perspectives to its readers. The organization is committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness in delivering information about international affairs.  They strive to provide a nuanced understanding of the world's evolving events.

articles.title: Iran ambassador hits out at ‘country to the north’ in US World Cup visa row | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s ambassador to Mexico, Abolfazl Pasandideh, criticized the United States for failing to provide visas to the Iranian national football team, claiming they are not competing on "equal terms" due to training difficulties.  He stated that the team is unable to train properly because of the ongoing US-Israel conflict and emphasized that the team will be playing in two West Coast US cities: Los Angeles and Seattle.

articles.title: Iran war live: Tehran, Trump yet to comment on 60-day truce extension plan | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran have reached an agreement to extend the ceasefire for 60 days, but President Donald Trump has yet to approve the memorandum of understanding.  Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned Israel's military actions against "peaceful people" in Lebanon.  The text of the MoU has not been finalized and a public announcement will be made once confirmed.

articles.title: US to designate two Brazilian gangs as ‘terrorist’ organisations | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has designated two Brazilian gangs, the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and the Comando Vermelho, as "terrorist" organizations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that these designations will block access to US assets for the groups starting June 5th. The decision is part of a broader push by the Trump administration to blur the lines between criminal and terrorist activity in Latin America. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has expressed concerns about the potential impact on Brazilian sovereignty and financial institutions, while Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who supports the designation, argues that it is necessary for public safety.

articles.title: Learning from Ukraine, Hezbollah is now using fibre-optic drones to hit Israel
articles.rephrased_article: Hezbollah is using fiber-optic drones to attack Israeli civilians and soldiers, increasing the threat in southern Lebanon. The drones, known as First-Person View or FPVs, are harder to detect than rockets or mortars and have caused significant casualties.  The Alma Research Center, an Israeli think tank, reports that Hezbollah has dozens of trained drone operators and a large stockpile of these inexpensive drones. Israel is struggling to counter the threat, with some officials acknowledging gaps in weapons development and focusing on destroying drones in warehouses or eliminating operators before launch. The conflict has intensified public pressure for decisive action from both sides.

articles.title: Afghan president voiced concern over civilians killed by SAS troops, inquiry told | British army | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: President Hamid Karzai expressed concerns about British special forces operations in Afghanistan, prompting a public inquiry into the deaths of up to 80 civilians. Evidence revealed that Afghan partner military units were reluctant to work alongside British special forces, and a review by a staff officer found the practice of separating Afghan males during raids was becoming counterproductive. The inquiry also heard allegations of civilian casualties caused by the SAS, including two adults shot dead while sleeping with children.  Concerns about the lethal conduct of the SAS in Helmand province led to the public inquiry, which has been slow-moving and shrouded in secrecy.

articles.title: Blond Bangladeshi buffalo nicknamed ‘Donald Trump’ saved from Eid sacrifice | Bangladesh | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh's home ministry intervened to save an albino buffalo nicknamed "Donald Trump" from being sacrificed for Eid al-Adha. The nearly 700kg animal, which had been sold for slaughter, was spared after a surge in public interest and security concerns arose. Salahuddin Ahmed, the minister of home affairs, ordered the buffalo be moved to the national zoo in Dhaka, refunded its buyer, and ensured its safety.  The unusual level of curiosity surrounding the albino buffalo's unique appearance likely saved it from being sacrificed.

articles.title: Down the Rabbit Hole: Bangladeshi buffalo 'Donald Trump' pardoned – a brief history of animal sacrifices | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A buffalo in Bangladesh, resembling Donald Trump, became an overnight sensation after being purchased for a large sum. The animal was spared from being sacrificed during Eid and will be sent to Dhaka's national zoo. This event echoes ancient practices where animals were often used as symbols of gods or sacrifices, demonstrating humanity's enduring fascination with the connection between nature and divinity.  The article explores how this tradition has evolved through various religions and cultures, highlighting the ongoing human tendency to find meaning in both sacrifice and pardon.

articles.title: Donald Trump shares draft Iran peace agreement with Israel and other allies | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has circulated a draft peace agreement with Iran among allies, including Israel, to prevent further escalation of the ceasefire. Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's foreign minister, will meet with Marco Rubio, his US counterpart, to expedite negotiations.  The draft agreement includes opening the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping, lifting the US blockade on Iranian ports, and providing Iran access to $12 billion in frozen assets. However, it lacks specifics about sanctions relief for Iran's oil and petrochemical exports and does not address a permanent ceasefire that would include Lebanon.  The fragile ceasefire remains precarious as tensions between Iran and the US escalate, with both sides refusing to cede ground on key points of disagreement.

articles.title: Gulf of suspicion: US and Iran said to be nearing deal even as missiles fly - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran negotiators have reached an agreement on a draft Memorandum of Understanding extending the fragile ceasefire and opening a 60-day negotiating window focused primarily on Iran's nuclear program in exchange for economic relief. President Donald Trump is reportedly considering the proposal, but has requested "a few days" to review it before making a decision. The proposed arrangement would mark the clearest sign yet that both Washington and Tehran recognize the limits of military escalation after months of naval warfare, sanctions, air strikes, and economic disruption.  The deal would see the ceasefire continue while unrestricted commercial shipping resumes through the Strait of Hormuz, with the US Navy lifting its blockade operations, Iranian harassment ceasing, and talks on sanctions relief, frozen Iranian funds, and humanitarian access to Iran commencing.

articles.title: Colombia’s first left-wing gov’t has reduced poverty, but has pile of debt | Elections | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Colombia's first left-wing government, led by Gustavo Petro, has implemented several social policies aimed at reducing poverty and inequality. These include tuition waivers for public university students, a minimum wage increase, and investments in renewable energy. However, the government also increased debt to fund these initiatives, which now presents a challenge for the next president. The incoming president will need to balance economic growth with social spending while addressing rising violence and trade tensions with Ecuador.  The election between Ivan Cepeda and Abelardo de la Espriella is expected to determine the future direction of Colombia's economy and social policies.

articles.title: British Museum postpones Jewish culture month lecture over protest fears | British Museum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The British Museum postponed a lecture on ancient Israel and Judah due to concerns about potential disruption by protesters. The museum, citing a "significant proportion" of registered attendees intending to disrupt the event, decided to reschedule the talk for early next month.  George Osborne, chair of the British Museum, shared the statement on X, while Kemi Badenoch, Conservative leader, called on the government to intervene and ensure the event's success. The decision drew criticism from Jewish commentators and free speech advocates who argued that publicly funded institutions should not retreat from hosting historical or cultural conversations relating to Jewish identity in response to protest threats.

articles.title: Ireland and Qatar halted twice by protests against upcoming Israel fixtures | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ireland and Qatar faced protests from fans opposing their upcoming fixtures against Israel.  The international football friendly between the Republic of Ireland and Qatar in Dublin was twice halted by home fan protests. The Irish parliament, the Dail, saw new protests over the Israel fixtures, while the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) requested UEFA suspend Israel from international competition. Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson challenged his players to "win this war" against Israel, and the first match between the sides will be played at a neutral venue on September 27th. The friendly match ended in a 1-0 win for the Irish with Collins’s header settling the match.

articles.title: Netanyahu orders Israeli army to seize ‘70% of Gaza Strip’, violating ceasefire deal | Gaza | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, has declared his intention to seize control of 70% of the Gaza Strip, threatening a fragile ceasefire and potentially creating catastrophic humanitarian conditions.  His directive follows Israel's steady expansion westward into Hamas-controlled territory since the October ceasefire, which saw Israel withdraw to a demarcation line granting it direct control of 53%. Israel Katz, the defense minister, has stated that the government aims for "voluntary migration" of Palestinians from Gaza, though human rights activists view this as an attempt at ethnic cleansing. This expansion would violate the ceasefire agreement and UN resolutions endorsing it, including Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan which outlined a temporary "yellow line" dividing Gaza into Israeli and Hamas-run halves.  Muhammad Shehada, a visiting fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, argues that Netanyahu is effectively nullifying the entire framework for Gaza established by the Trump administration.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: JD Vance says US ‘not there yet’ on an Iran deal amid question over nuclear program | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Vance stated that while the US is close to reaching an agreement with Iran, he cannot guarantee its success.  Tasnim news agency reported that a potential memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the two countries has not yet been finalized or confirmed, and Donald Trump circulated a draft peace agreement among allies including Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered his army to seize control of 70% of the Gaza Strip, threatening an already fragile ceasefire and escalating humanitarian conditions in the devastated territory.  Lebanon's prime minister condemned Israel's ongoing assault on the south, calling for an immediate ceasefire. Meanwhile, Iranian state TV reported that Iranian forces intercepted and destroyed a US aircraft near Iran’s southern Bushehr province.

articles.title: Tense protests erupt outside Delaney Hall immigrant detention centre in US | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Protests erupted outside the Delaney Hall immigrant detention center in New Jersey following a hunger strike by detainees. Governor Mikie Sherrill and members of Congress, including Jerry Nadler, Daniel Goldman, and Adriano Espaillat, have visited the facility and reported dire conditions, including medical neglect and spoiled food.  The Department of Homeland Security claims that protesters assaulted federal agents, while critics question the charges filed against them. The center is run by a private contractor, GEO Group, under contract with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

articles.title: NASA to reveal Artemis III crew as Moon mission preparations gather pace | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA will unveil the crew members for its Artemis III mission on June 9th during a live broadcast from the Johnson Space Center in Houston. The announcement, made via NASA+ and YouTube, will also include an update on the mission's progress and limited interviews with the selected astronauts.  The Artemis III mission is part of NASA’s Artemis program, which aims to conduct critical rendezvous and docking operations for future lunar landings and exploration.

articles.title: Latvia parliament approves new gov’t after drone dispute toppled coalition | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Latvia’s parliament approved a new coalition government led by 47-year-old centrist Andris Kulbergs, who will serve until October's parliamentary elections. The move comes after the previous government collapsed following an argument over its handling of stray drones suspected to be from Ukraine. President Edgars Rinkevics backed opposition lawmaker Kulbergs, citing the need for a pro-EU, pro-NATO direction and strong military reinforcement in light of multiple Russian and Ukrainian drone incidents within the country.

articles.title: Indian-origin founder in Canada says people talk about H-1B as if Indians randomly woke up one day, booked flights, started taking US jobs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vijayan Swaminathan, an Indian-origin tech leader in Canada, criticized the portrayal of H-1B visa holders as "random" job seekers. He argued that these individuals are often experienced engineers who have spent years working on specific projects for American corporations and that hiring them is a strategic decision to expedite development timelines. Swaminathan emphasized that the question should be directed at companies making hiring decisions, not individual workers, and highlighted the cultural exchange between the US and India through popular media and food industries.

articles.title: What’s behind South Africa’s anti-migrant protests? | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa is experiencing renewed anti-immigrant protests, with groups demanding the departure of foreign workers by June 30. These protests stem from accusations that many foreign nationals are residing and working illegally in the country. South African citizens argue that the government has not effectively enforced immigration laws, leading to frustration and calls for stricter measures.  The issue highlights a longstanding tension between economic needs and social anxieties surrounding immigration in South Africa.

articles.title: Trump administration sues states for denying ICE agents undercover plates | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has filed lawsuits against four states, Maine, Massachusetts, Oregon, and Washington, for refusing to issue confidential license plates to ICE agents. The Department of Justice argues that these plates are necessary for the safety and operational effectiveness of ICE agents who face harassment. However, the states contend that such secrecy undermines oversight and public accountability.  The clash highlights a broader debate over federal immigration enforcement powers and the role of state governments in regulating them.

articles.title: EU sanctions ‘extremist’ Israeli settlers in occupied West Bank | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union has sanctioned 136 individuals and 41 entities from various countries for alleged human rights abuses against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. The sanctions target groups like the Nachala Settlement Movement, its director Daniella Weiss, and Regavim and its director Meir Deutsch, who are accused of promoting forced displacement and demolition of Palestinian property.  The EU also sanctioned the Hashomer Yosh NGO and its president Avichai Suissa, for supporting violent outposts and settlements, and the Amana cooperative association of the settler movement Gush Emunim. The sanctions come after a long delay due to Hungary's former Prime Minister Viktor Orban's veto.

articles.title: 'Sorry pal, this is how rest of the world travels': American journalist shows chaos at Lisbon Airport due to new EU rules, gets trolled - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union's Entry/Exit System (EES), designed to register non-EU nationals traveling for short stays, has faced significant challenges since its April rollout. The system requires biometric data collection, leading to long queues and disruptions at airports, as seen in Lisbon where CNN journalist Clarissa Ward missed her flight due to the wait time. Airlines are urging airport authorities to suspend the measures during peak travel season, while some social media users argue that this is a common experience for travelers worldwide.

articles.title: Clashes between armed groups in Colombia kill at least 52 | Colombia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pedro Sánchez, the defense minister, confirmed fighting in the jungles of Guaviare, Colombia, between rival armed groups vying for control of a cocaine production region. Iván Mordisco, leader of a dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), and Alexander Díaz Mendoza, leader of another Farc faction, are involved in the clashes, which have resulted in at least 52 deaths according to the dissidents.  The fighting is part of a long-standing conflict fueled by drug trafficking and illegal mining that has claimed over 450,000 lives and displaced millions.

articles.title: 21-year-old Austrian man sentenced to 15 years for planning ISIS-inspired terror attack at Taylor Swift concert - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 21-year-old Austrian man, identified as Beran A, was sentenced to 15 years in prison for planning a terror attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. Beran A had pledged allegiance to the Islamic State group and planned to use knives or homemade explosives to attack concertgoers. The plot was thwarted by authorities who received a tip-off from the CIA, and nearly 200,000 fans were expected to attend the canceled concerts.  The case attracted international attention as it targeted Swift's record-breaking Eras Tour.

articles.title: International Day of Markhor passes unnoticed in Chitral - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Day of the Markhor, established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2024, was not celebrated in Chitral this year. Local wildlife officials failed to organize any events or ceremonies despite hosting the largest population of Kashmir Markhor in Pakistan's national park.  Ecologists expressed disappointment over the lack of official recognition and highlighted the significance of the day for global conservation efforts.

articles.title: Guatemala denies agreeing to US strikes against drug traffickers | Military News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Guatemala's government denies agreeing to allow the United States to carry out strikes against drug traffickers, despite seeking security cooperation with Washington. The statement comes in response to a New York Times report that cited two unidentified sources claiming President Bernardo Arevalo had agreed to US military action in his country.  The Guatemalan government emphasized that their request for assistance was not an invitation for US attacks and falls within existing bilateral agreements on security cooperation.

articles.title: Guatemala requests US military cooperation against drug trafficking | Guatemala | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Guatemala's president, Bernardo Arévalo, requested US military cooperation in combating drug trafficking. The request includes access to equipment, training, and experts, but does not authorize foreign military operations on Guatemalan soil.  The agreement falls under existing bilateral agreements, as confirmed by the US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth. The Pentagon intends to work with Honduras to expand this cooperation, according to a spokesperson. The move comes amid broader White House efforts to normalize US military presence in Latin America and gain leverage over Mexico.

articles.title: US and Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire, US officials say
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for 60 days, with negotiations on the future of Iran's nuclear program to follow. The framework, yet to be approved by President Donald Trump or Iranian leadership, includes lifting the US naval blockade of Iran's ports and allowing unrestricted passage through the Strait of Hormuz.  However, both sides have accused each other of ceasefire violations, and the White House has not confirmed an agreement.

articles.title: UN ‘adds Israel to blacklist’ for conflict-related sexual violence | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations has added Israel to its blacklist of parties suspected of or responsible for sexual violence in conflict zones.  Israeli ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, announced that Israel will sever ties with the UN secretary-general, Antonio Guterres, over the upcoming report. The decision was met with anger from the Israeli government and foreign ministry, who accused the UN of being politicized and corrupt.  The UN has cited credible information regarding sexual violence committed by Israeli security forces against Palestinian detainees in prisons and detention centers, prompting a response from Israel that it will sue the New York Times for reporting on alleged rape by its forces.

articles.title: UK minister visits Australia for ‘lessons’ ahead of expected British social media crackdown | Social media | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kanishka Narayan, the UK’s online safety minister, spent a week in Australia learning from the country's under-16s social media ban.  The UK government is expected to announce its own crackdown on social media for teens within weeks after a public consultation. Julie Inman Grant, the eSafety commissioner of Australia, has reported that two-thirds of teenagers have remained on social media since the ban came into effect in December. The UK and Australia signed a memorandum of understanding this week to share information about frontier AI models and cyber-attacks.  The UK government is prioritizing building its own internal capabilities for cybersecurity rather than relying on companies.

articles.title: N Korea not keen to engage with the US or S Korea: Singapore FM - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Vivian Balakrishnan, Singapore's foreign minister, stated that North Korea is focused on strengthening its self-reliance and military capabilities, while rejecting reunification with South Korea. He noted that Kim Jong Un’s regime has deepened ties with Russia and China, but remains hesitant to engage in significant communication with the United States, South Korea, or Japan.  Balakrishnan also highlighted Pyongyang's development despite its isolation, suggesting it could be integrated into a wider regional network.

articles.title: NCCIA Punjab arrests 11 for 'anti-state propaganda' and 'inciting unrest' online - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in Punjab, Pakistan arrested 11 individuals accused of spreading anti-state propaganda and inciting unrest through social media.  The arrests were made across multiple cities, including Lahore, Faisalabad, Multan, and Gujranwala. NCCIA Director Muhammad Ali Waseem stated that the suspects will be prosecuted under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), 2016, with no leniency shown towards those involved in such activities.

articles.title: US and Iran reach tentative deal for 60-day truce extension, officials say | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran reached a tentative memorandum of understanding (MOU) to extend the 60-day ceasefire for further negotiations. The agreement, which requires President Donald Trump's final approval, would address vessel traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and lift the US naval blockade on Iranian ports.  However, details remain unclear, including whether the extension represents a deadline. Iran has denied reports of an imminent deal while reiterating its commitment to not pursuing nuclear weapons. The MOU also requires Iran to refrain from pursuing a nuclear weapon, but other sticking points, such as sanctions and uranium stockpile limits, need further discussion.

articles.title: Rebuilding US weapons stockpile may ‘take years’ post-Iran war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) report states that rebuilding US munitions inventories, depleted during the Iran war, will take at least two years. The report highlights four critical munitions heavily used in the conflict – Land Attack Missile (TLAM), Terminal High Altitude Area Defences (THAAD) interceptors, Patriot missiles, and SM-3 and SM-6 ship-based surface-to-air missiles – that require replenishment.  The CSIS report also notes that decisions on new production allocation have created bilateral friction and will continue for several years as demand outpaces supply.

articles.title: Dar invites overseas Pakistanis in US to 'honour their roots' and invest in the country - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed Pakistani-American community leaders in New York, highlighting Pakistan's economic progress and inviting investment. He emphasized the government's efforts to stabilize the economy, improve credit ratings, and strengthen investor confidence. Dar also spoke about Pakistan's recent military victories against India and its role in promoting peace between the US and Iran.  He concluded by stating that Pakistan is poised for a bright future.

articles.title: Israel’s Netanyahu directs army to seize 70 percent of Gaza Strip | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, has ordered his army to seize 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, expanding control beyond the agreed-upon "Yellow Line" demarcated in a ceasefire agreement. This expansion follows the Israeli army's quiet mapping of its expanded territory, which now controls about 11 percent more than the designated area. The move comes amidst ongoing violence and humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where Palestinians face dire conditions including limited access to resources and frequent attacks from Israel.  The UN Office for Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has reported a critical humanitarian situation in Gaza with widespread displacement and inadequate sanitation.

articles.title: Carney calls for new US-Canada partnership to ‘help make America great again’ | Mark Carney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Carney, Canada's prime minister, called for a stronger partnership with the United States during a speech in New York. He emphasized the need for a "true partnership" to address global competition and highlighted Canada's efforts to diversify its trade relationships beyond the US.  Carney argued that increased strategic autonomy is crucial in today's interconnected world and criticized Trump's actions, including tariffs and threats of annexation. The Canadian prime minister also stressed the importance of collaboration on critical minerals and energy resources for both countries' economic growth and national security.

articles.title: EU fines Temu for failing to stop sale of illegal and dangerous products | European Commission | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The European Commission has fined Temu, a Chinese shopping website, €200 million for failing to prevent the sale of illegal and dangerous products. The fine is the second-highest ever imposed under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) and follows a 19-month investigation that found unsafe products on the platform, including baby toys, electronics, and clothing. Temu has the right to appeal the decision and claims it disagrees with the fine's proportionality. The company says it is taking steps to strengthen risk assessment and user protection.

articles.title: US Treasury threatens Oman with sanctions over Hormuz Strait | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Oman that the US will impose sanctions if it facilitates tolls in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions between the two countries.  Bessent stated that Washington "will not tolerate" any fees imposed on commercial ships in the strategic waterway and emphasized that all nations should reject Iran's efforts to disrupt commerce. This follows President Donald Trump's threats against Oman, a key US ally known for its neutrality, over potential Iranian-Omani control of the Strait.  The US has been indirectly negotiating with Iran to reach an agreement for a comprehensive end to the war, and control over the Hormuz Strait has emerged as a major point of disagreement.

articles.title: Govt. plans security protocol for fishing harbours under CISF oversight - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will oversee the security of around 1,200 fishing harbours and landing sites across India as part of a plan to strengthen the country's coastline. The Union Home Ministry aims to implement this framework after assigning CISF personnel to secure 250 seaports. This move follows guidelines issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) in 2023, and is intended to provide a uniform security template for all coastal areas.  The government's objective is to ensure the safety of fisherfolk and prevent potential threats like those seen during the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.

articles.title: Trump's face could appear on US $250 bill - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's likeness is being considered for a new $250 bill, a proposal that would be the first time a living person appears on US currency in over 150 years.  The Treasury Department, under the Trump administration, has pushed forward with the plan despite concerns about federal law prohibiting depictions of living presidents on money. The printing bureau director, Patricia Solimene, was reassigned after raising objections to the proposal. This move has sparked criticism from Democrats and accusations of a cult of personality around the 79-year-old leader.

articles.title: Israel hits Lebanese capital Beirut in 'targeted strike'
articles.rephrased_article: Israel carried out a targeted strike on the Lebanese capital, Beirut, for the second time since a ceasefire last month. The IDF stated that the attack was in response to Hezbollah attacks and aimed at Ali al-Husni, head of an Iranian militia.  The strikes came after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced an expansion of a ground operation following Hezbollah drone attacks on troops and civilians. At least 11 people were killed in two sets of Israeli strikes which hit Tyre and an area to the city's east early on Thursday. The escalation threatens to derail peace talks between the US, Israel, and Iran, while Lebanon faces displacement and humanitarian concerns.

articles.title: Image of Thai police in sparkly dresses with handcuffed suspect turns out to be AI fake | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Thai police officers posted an image of themselves in elaborate festival-style dresses arresting a drug dealer on their Facebook page.  However, the image was later revealed to be an AI-generated fake, prompting media outlets to retract their stories and highlighting the challenges of verifying images online. The incident underscores the need for improved verification methods as AI-generated imagery becomes increasingly prevalent.

articles.title: US, Mexico, Canada announce Ebola-related travel measures for World Cup | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US, Mexico, and Canada have announced aligned public health travel measures for individuals coming from African regions at risk of Ebola as the World Cup begins next month. The WHO declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo a public health emergency of international concern, prompting governments to implement containment measures.  The measures include bans on entry for certain citizens and residents, as well as quarantine requirements for those who have been in affected areas recently.

articles.title: Pakistan, China agree to deepen military cooperation: Chinese Defense Ministry - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: China and Pakistan reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening military cooperation during a recent high-level exchange.  Colonel Jiang Bin, Chinese Defence Ministry Spokesman, highlighted the close ties between the two countries, emphasizing practical cooperation in areas such as joint exercises, training, and technology sharing. He expressed China's willingness to deepen strategic communication and support each other on core interests, aiming to build a closer China-Pakistan community with shared future goals of regional and global peace, development, and security.

articles.title: Are US and Iran close to peace or sliding back to war?
articles.rephrased_article: The US and Iran are navigating a tense ceasefire after weeks of conflict, with both sides accusing the other of violating the agreement.  Iran responded to recent US strikes by attacking an American air base, while US Central Command (Centcom) reported intercepting a ballistic missile launched from Iran. Despite escalating tensions, neither side appears interested in resuming full-scale war. Diplomatic efforts led by Pakistan are ongoing but have yet to produce a comprehensive agreement on key issues like the nuclear program and the future of the Strait of Hormuz.  The fragile ceasefire remains intact for now, with both sides expressing their willingness to avoid further escalation.

articles.title: EU to discuss potential restrictions on Chinese imports amid fears of overreliance | European Commission | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: EU commissioners will meet on Friday to discuss new restrictions on imports from China, dubbed "China Shock 2.0," due to concerns about the impact of Chinese imports on European industries. The meeting aims to align the commission's thinking and address overproduction in China, which is leading to cheaper prices for EU consumers.  Ignacio García Bercero, a senior fellow at Bruegel, suggests using quotas and tariff rate quotas as potential solutions. He emphasizes the need for a clear strategy and engagement with China.

articles.title: Dar to meet Rubio in Washington tomorrow: FO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, will meet with Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and National Security Advisor, in Washington on Friday. The meeting was rescheduled from today to discuss bilateral relations, regional and global developments, and cooperation in key sectors.  Dar's visit comes amid escalating tensions between the US and Iran following a cabinet meeting chaired by President Donald Trump, who is seeking progress towards a peace deal with Tehran.

articles.title: Gaza City hospitals say several killed in strike, as Israel targets Hamas leaders
articles.rephrased_article: Israel targeted a building in Gaza City, killing at least 10 people, including five children, according to Gaza City hospitals. The attack reportedly targeted a Hamas battalion commander, Imad Asleem, and his daughter Israa.  The Israeli military stated they struck "two central Hamas terrorists" but did not disclose their identities. This latest strike follows several other attacks targeting senior Hamas figures in recent days.  The violence comes amidst ongoing indirect US-brokered talks between Israel and Hamas aimed at advancing President Trump's peace plan for Gaza, which includes the Palestinian armed group giving up its weapons and Israeli troop withdrawals.

articles.title: Israel intensifies attacks on southern Lebanon, killing at least 16 people | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel intensified its attacks on southern Lebanon, killing at least 16 people and wounding 58 in a series of airstrikes targeting residential areas, roads, and civilian infrastructure. Hezbollah has been designated as the target of these strikes, but Israeli forces have also hit populated areas, forcing thousands to flee under threat of attack. The International Committee of the Red Cross warned that the escalating violence is deepening a humanitarian crisis, with fears that conditions will worsen.  These attacks came despite a US-brokered ceasefire that took effect last month and are casting doubt on the prospects for diplomacy between Israel and Lebanon.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Civilian casualties and displacement are reported as routine in the conflict.

articles.title: EU fines Temu €200m for allowing sale of illegal products
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union has fined Temu, a Chinese-owned online retailer, €200 million for selling illegal products such as baby toys and faulty chargers. The fine stems from an investigation into whether Temu is meeting its obligations under EU law as a designated Very Large Online Platform.  Temu disagrees with the decision and considers the fine disproportionate, while the European Commission stated that the penalty aims to send a strong message about compliance.

articles.title: Argentina’s ‘European’ self-image under renewed scrutiny after racist incidents in Brazil | Argentina | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Brazilian woman was horrified when a fellow passenger on a train revealed an Argentinian tourist had been secretly filming her seven-year-old son. The man, Eduardo Ignacio Murias, 63, admitted to sending the photos to a WhatsApp contact and wrote racist messages about the child. He was arrested for "racial insult" and faces legal repercussions in both countries. This incident has reignited debate about racism, national identity, and Argentina's long history of racial prejudice, particularly as Argentinian tourists are increasingly visiting Brazil.

articles.title: Princess Diana: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: “Carry out a random act of kindness, with no expectation of reward, safe in the knowledge that one day someone might do the same for you.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Princess Diana's quote, "Carry out a random act of kindness, with no expectation of reward, safe in the knowledge that one day someone might do the same for you," continues to resonate decades later because it emphasizes the power of small acts of kindness.  The quote encourages people to engage in simple gestures without expecting immediate recognition or return, highlighting the potential for these actions to create positive ripples in the world.  This message resonates with individuals who may feel overwhelmed by larger societal issues, reminding them that even seemingly insignificant acts can have a profound impact on others' emotional well-being.

articles.title: 200 personnel from Federal Constabulary's diplomatic protection unit to receive training in Saudi Arabia - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Saudi counterpart, Abdulaziz bin Saud Al Saud, met in Mina, Saudi Arabia to discuss bilateral relations and internal security matters.  During the meeting, they agreed that 200 personnel from the Federal Constabulary’s Special Diplomatic Protection Unit will receive training in Saudi Arabia. The ministers also discussed the current regional situation, with Al Saud praising Pakistan's role in reducing tensions.

articles.title: For Gaza, Eid joy is now a form of resistance | Gaza | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite the ongoing Israeli blockade and high prices, Gaza residents celebrated Eid al-Adha with a mix of joy and sorrow.  The celebration was marred by Israeli attacks on the Remal neighborhood that killed six people and injured 20 others.  While many families struggled to afford basic necessities, they continued to hold onto their traditions, including the ritual sacrifice of animals, hoping for an end to the suffering in Gaza.  Despite these challenges, Gaza residents remain resilient and continue to celebrate life as a form of resistance against the occupation.

articles.title: Family accuse FCDO of lack of support over death of UK man in Grenada | Grenada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The family of Andrew Frederick, a British man found dead in Grenada, is accusing UK authorities of failing to support their fight for justice. The family claims that despite evidence indicating homicide, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) refused to refer their case to its murder and manslaughter team, citing "discretion" and lack of guidance.  Eve Henderson, co-founder of Murdered Abroad, a charity assisting the family, expressed shock at the UK's reluctance to offer support, highlighting the significant number of homicides of British nationals abroad annually.  The Metropolitan Police stated they do not publicly comment on investigations led by other police forces.

articles.title: Princess Diana: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: “Carry out a random act of kindness, with no expectation of reward, safe in the knowledge that one day someone might do the same for you.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Diana, Princess of Wales's quote about carrying out random acts of kindness without expectation of reward remains popular because it emphasizes the value and potential ripple effect of small gestures. The quote resonates with people who feel overwhelmed by modern life's complexities and seek reminders of human connection and compassion.  It encourages a belief in goodness that may eventually return, even if not immediately recognized or rewarded.

articles.title: Pentagon says US military personnel reportedly being targeted using location data - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: US Central Command (Centcom) has confirmed that military personnel have been targeted by adversaries using commercially available location data in active war zones.  The disclosure, made in a letter to the Pentagon from Senator Ron Wyden and a bipartisan group of legislators, highlights the growing concern over the use of this data for surveillance and attack planning. The lawmakers urged the Pentagon to take immediate action to protect personnel, such as disabling unique advertising IDs on military devices and steering staff away from privacy-compromising browsers like Google's Chrome.  The issue has raised concerns about the potential national security risks posed by the commercial location data trade.

articles.title: Iran says US must issue multiple-entry visas for its World Cup squad | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s football federation president, Mehdi Taj, stated that the team requires multiple-entry visas for their US World Cup matches.  Taj explained that the team will need to re-enter the US several times during the tournament and expects the US to issue these visas. The team's base camp has been relocated from the US to Mexico, with FIFA approving the change after a request by Iran.  The Iranian squad is scheduled to play three group stage matches in the United States.

articles.title: Dormitory fire at Kenyan girls’ school kills at least 16 students | Kenya | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at Utumishi girls academy in Gilgil, Kenya, has killed at least 16 students and injured 79 others. The cause of the blaze is still under investigation, but it occurred around 3:30 am on Thursday morning while approximately 220 students were sleeping in a dormitory.  The Kenya Red Cross reported that several students have been evacuated to hospitals for treatment, and police are searching for those who may have escaped. Dozens of parents gathered at the school seeking information about their children.

articles.title: Iran and US trade attacks after Trump rejects report of Hormuz agreement | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following US attacks near Bandar Abbas airport, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a US base in retaliation.  An unnamed US official said the US military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station. The ceasefire remains fragile as negotiations to end the war drag on, with both sides expressing confidence that they are not yet ready to collapse the agreement. Donald Trump rejected an Iranian report of a deal restoring commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz within a month, while Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Iranian parliament's national security committee, stated that Iran will not back down from its demands for uranium enrichment and sanctions relief.

articles.title: Oil prices jump after US launches new attacks on Iran
articles.rephrased_article: US forces conducted new airstrikes on Iran, targeting a military site in Bandar Abbas, a strategic port city. The attacks came despite a ceasefire between the two countries and raised oil prices globally. Brent crude rose by 3.75% to $97.83 (£73.15) per barrel, while US-traded crude was 4% higher at $92.22.  The strikes have escalated tensions in the region and threaten global energy supplies.

articles.title: Kaja Kallas warns against walking into Russian ‘trap’ as EU ministers meet for talks – Europe live | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign policy chief, warned against focusing on personalities in potential peace talks with Russia and urged the bloc to prioritize substance over individuals. She cautioned against falling into a Russian trap by discussing who would lead negotiations, emphasizing that the EU must be represented regardless of the chosen negotiator.  Several EU ministers are divided on appointing a single negotiator for Russia, with some advocating for a team effort while others prefer a more neutral approach. Péter Magyar, Hungary's new prime minister, is in Brussels to discuss frozen EU funds, but his visit has been overshadowed by ongoing negotiations over Orbán-era reforms.

articles.title: Mike Marshall: Meet Mike Marshall: The former soldier graduating at 69 after leaving school with no qualifications at 15 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mike Marshall, a 69-year-old former soldier and police officer, is graduating with a 2:1 in History from the University of East Anglia.  He left school at 15 without qualifications and pursued a career in public service before returning to education as a mature student. After an unexpected conversation with a university admissions staff member, Marshall enrolled and overcame initial challenges to achieve top grades. He plans to pursue a history-focused tour across Europe after graduation and considers further studies.  Marshall's journey exemplifies determination, lifelong learning, and second chances.

articles.title: Australia charges alleged ISIL-linked woman after return from Syria | ISIL/ISIS News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Australia has charged a 34-year-old woman with alleged links to the ISIL group after she returned from Syria. The woman faces charges of being a member of a "terrorist" organization and entering a declared conflict zone, potentially resulting in up to 10 years imprisonment. Police are investigating all adult returnees, including three women who face additional charges, including crimes against humanity.  The repatriation of these individuals follows the return of women and children from Syrian detention camps without trial.

articles.title: US firm fined for Australian immigration security failures. How much? Border force refuses to say | Australian immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian Border Force (ABF) has penalized private prison company MTC, which runs Australian immigration detention centers, after a series of security failures including escapes and staff injuries. The ABF commissioner refused to disclose the financial penalties imposed on Secure Journeys, a subsidiary of MTC, citing commercial confidentiality. Senator David Shoebridge criticized the government's handling of the situation, questioning why details of the fines were being withheld from public view.  The investigation revealed numerous incidents, including detainees missing medical appointments due to staffing shortages and staff being hospitalized after attempting to rescue an unconscious detainee from a fire.

articles.title: What does NEET mean and why is Britain facing a ‘lost generation’ of 1.25m young people? | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Britain is facing a growing concern over the number of young people classified as "NEET," not in education, employment, or training. A review led by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn warns that the number could rise by 25% to 1.25 million by early 2030s unless urgent action is taken. The report highlights a combination of fewer entry-level jobs, mental health challenges, and economic pressure as contributing factors to the increase in NEET levels. Business groups have also warned that higher employment costs are discouraging companies from hiring younger workers.

articles.title: US strikes Iran, drawing retaliatory attack on American base after Trump dismisses report of Hormuz deal - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for targeting a US airbase after the US military carried out strikes against Iranian drones near the Strait of Hormuz. The escalation in hostilities, which followed President Donald Trump's rejection of a report on a potential compromise deal with Tehran, heightened tensions and sent oil prices surging again.  The US official involved in the military operations stated that the actions were defensive and aimed at maintaining the ceasefire between the two countries.

articles.title: World Cup delegation compliant with US Ebola protocols, DR Congo says | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) football federation and FIFA confirmed that its World Cup delegation is compliant with US protocols related to the Ebola outbreak, clearing the way for the team to compete. The delegation has cancelled a training camp in Kinshasa and relocated preparations abroad, ensuring compliance with health and safety measures. DRC Ambassador to the US Yvette Kapinga Ngandu expressed confidence in the team's readiness and safety, while Sports Minister Didier Budimbu highlighted the government's efforts to ensure their preparedness for the tournament.

articles.title: US returns Palestinian rights expert Francesca Albanese to sanctions list | United Nations News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States government reinstated Francesca Albanese, a UN expert on Palestinian rights, to the sanctions list after a judge temporarily blocked the designation. The Trump administration had previously sanctioned Albanese for her criticism of Israeli policies and recommendations to the International Criminal Court (ICC).  Albanese's family filed a lawsuit against the sanctions, arguing they hindered her life and freedom of speech. A three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit issued an administrative stay on the lower court injunction, allowing the government to reinstate the designation.

articles.title: Australia sues 3M over 'forever chemicals' in firefighting foam
articles.rephrased_article: Australia is suing 3M, a US manufacturing giant, for AU$2 billion in damages over the alleged use of toxic "forever chemicals" in firefighting foam that contaminated dozens of defense bases. The government claims 3M withheld information about the foam's environmental impact and misled them about its safety, despite knowing otherwise.  3M denies making PFAS in Australia and stopped selling the foam there 20 years ago.

articles.title: Lashkar-E-Taiba: LeT turns on its Pakistan masters over recognising Israel - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saifullah Kasuri, deputy chief of Lashkar-e-Taiba, threatened Pakistan's frontline leadership and military officials with assassination if they recognized Israel, escalating tensions following President Trump's call for diplomatic ties.  Kasuri made these threats during a rally in response to the Abraham Accords, claiming no international power could coerce Muslim nations into accepting Israeli statehood. He emphasized Pakistan's growing defense alliance with Saudi Arabia as a countermeasure against Israeli influence and used inflammatory rhetoric about jihad and Palestine.

articles.title: Oil prices bounce higher after new US strikes on Iran - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged on Thursday, driven by renewed US strikes against Iran, erasing Wednesday's declines.  Iranian forces fired at four ships in the Strait of Hormuz, while Kuwait reported air defense responses to missile and drone attacks. Despite an Iranian official stating renewed hostilities were unlikely, US President Donald Trump threatened to "finish the job" if a peace deal wasn't reached. This volatile situation has led to mixed signals regarding the fragile ceasefire in the Middle East war, which continues to impact global energy markets. Asian stock markets mostly fell, with South Korean chipmaker SK hynix hitting a $1 trillion market capitalization.

articles.title: Australia charges woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State
articles.rephrased_article: Australia has charged a 34-year-old woman, identified as Rayann El Houli, with being a member of the terrorist organization Islamic State and entering a declared conflict zone.  The woman arrived in Australia last September after spending time in Syria's al-Hawl camp.  Hilda Sirec, federal police assistant commissioner, stated that all adult women who returned recently are under investigation.

articles.title: Oil Price Today (May 28): Crude oil surges nearly 3% after Iran says it targeted US airbase in retaliation for fresh American strikes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility for striking a US airbase, while US Central Command responded with strikes on an Iranian ground control station.  Oil prices surged as the situation escalated, with Brent crude reaching $97.29 per barrel and WTI crude at $91.71. Despite progress in negotiations between Washington and Tehran, uncertainty remains, leading to cautious responses from central banks. Analysts warn that even a deal may take months to normalize shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Strait Of Hormuz: 'War left regime desperate for cash': US sanctions authority overseeing Strait of Hormuz as Middle East conflict enters 90th day - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US administration imposed new sanctions on Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority, targeting the agency overseeing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The move comes after US forces carried out strikes on an Iranian military facility following the downing of Iranian attack drones.  Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, stated that these sanctions are a result of Iran's desperate attempt to extort global maritime trade. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard defended the move, asserting that ships must follow designated routes through the waterway. The conflict has caused disruptions in oil and gas supplies, pushing prices up globally.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz says Youm-i-Takbeer symbolises Pakistan's strength, sovereignty and national unity - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari both acknowledged the significance of May 28, 1998, as a defining moment in Pakistan's history. This day marked the successful completion of nuclear tests by Pakistan, which restored strategic balance in South Asia in response to India's nuclear ambitions.  The leaders praised the scientists, engineers, armed forces personnel, and workers who contributed to this historic achievement. They also highlighted Pakistan's commitment to national security and its right to self-defense while emphasizing the importance of unity and resilience in facing future challenges.

articles.title: US strikes Iran targets for second time in three days
articles.rephrased_article: The US military conducted new strikes on an Iranian military site in Bandar Abbas, a strategic port city. The strikes followed previous attacks on Iranian missile sites and boats in the Strait of Hormuz, which were also described as self-defense measures.  Iran condemned these actions as a violation of the ceasefire and vowed to retaliate. President Donald Trump stated that Iran is "negotiating on fumes" and threatened to resume a large-scale bombing campaign if an agreement is not reached.
